name: Metro Nature in Neighborhoods Community Stewardship and Restoration Grants
summary: Grants from the Portland-area regional government for community-led habitat restoration and stewardship projects on public or protected land, requiring partnerships of at least three organisations.

amount.note: Small grants up to $50,000, medium up to $75,000, large up to $100,000.

fiscal_sponsor.note: The sponsor has nonprofit or other tax-exempt status

eligibility.rule: Have nonprofit or tax-exempt status, or a fiscal sponsor with that status
Address at least one of the program goals
Occur on public or permanently protected land within the Metro boundary, with a few exceptions
If on private land, show a clear public and environmental benefit
Not replace required mitigation or penalty payments or produce direct profit or proprietary resources
Have written landowner permission at the time of full application

documents: Location/vicinity map of up to two pages

status.quote: Tuesday, April 21st, 2026 Final applications due to Metro by 4 p.m.

deadline.quote: Pre-applications are due by 4 p.m. February 10, 2026.

pool.quote: Members of the review committee will help to allocate up to $750,000 in community stewardship and restoration grants

applicant_types.quote: Community groups, watershed councils, neighborhood associations, nonprofits, faith groups and service groups with nonprofit or other tax-exempt status may apply.

geography.quote: Grants may only be awarded to projects and programs that benefit Metro-area residents.

access.quote: Make an appointment to talk with the program manager.

window.quote: These grants are currently offered every other year; this is the second community stewardship and restoration grant opportunity of the 2022 levy renewal.

amount.quote: Small grants have a maximum award of $50,000, medium grants have a maximum award of $75,000, and large grants have a maximum award of $100,000.

consortium_required.quote: Therefore, this grant program requires each application to have at least three partners (including the lead applicant).

fiscal_sponsor.quote: Community groups, watershed councils, collectives, neighborhood associations, nonprofits, faith groups and service groups with nonprofit or other tax exempt status, or with a fiscal sponsor who has that status may apply.

effort.quote: Pre-applications are due by 4 p.m. February 10, 2026.
Tuesday, April 21st, 2026 Final applications due to Metro by 4 p.m.

eligibility.quote: Community groups, watershed councils, collectives, neighborhood associations, nonprofits, faith groups and service groups with nonprofit or other tax exempt status, or with a fiscal sponsor who has that status may apply.
Projects must address at least one of the program goals (see below).

Projects must occur on publicly-owned or permanently protected lands, such as land trust property, within the metropolitan-area urban growth boundary or Metro's jurisdictional boundary, with a few exceptions.
Projects on private land must be able to show a clear public and environmental benefit.
All projects must benefit Metro region residents.
Projects cannot take the place of required mitigation or penalty payments or result in direct profit or proprietary resources.
All projects must have written landowner permission at the time of full application.

after_award.quote: Grantees will describe the successes and challenges of their program to Metro staff every six months through the submission of a progress report and/or a site visit and the submission of one final report at the completion of the grant contract.

documents.quote: Upload a location/vicinity map of up to two pages that shows where the project and/or participating communities are located within the region.
